boards.school_name: Citadel Military College of South Carolina
boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Citadel Military College of South Carolina
boards.description: Late-night dining for Citadel cadets is defined by strict leave windows and the midnight gate closure. These spots provide essential fuel during weekend general leave or via delivery for upperclassmen.

cards.title: The On-Campus Standard
cards.subtitle: Mark Clark Hall
cards.notes: Located in the student center, this is the primary retail option for cadets. It serves as a reliable hub for chicken sandwiches and shakes before evening formations.
cards.short_summary: The central on-campus retail dining option for cadets located in Mark Clark Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Chick-fil-A is located in Mark Clark Hall and is a fully licensed location serving the campus.
cards.source_title: Retail Dining - Auxiliary Services - The Citadel
cards.access_notes: Open until 7:00 PM on weekdays and 4:00 PM on Saturdays; closed Sundays.

cards.title: The Jumbo Slice Run
cards.subtitle: Upper King Street
cards.notes: Famous for massive 28-inch pizzas, this spot is a go-to for cadets on weekend leave. The jumbo slices are a high-calorie staple for those returning before the midnight curfew.
cards.short_summary: A popular pizza shop on King Street known for serving exceptionally large slices late into the night.
cards.evidence_claim: Benny Ravello's is open until 1:00 AM Sunday-Wednesday and 2:00 AM Thursday-Saturday.
cards.source_title: Benny Ravello's
cards.access_notes: Open until 2:00 AM on Friday and Saturday nights.

cards.title: The Post-Leave Tray
cards.subtitle: Savannah Highway
cards.notes: A short drive from campus, Cook Out is the ultimate late-night destination for its 'Trays' and 40+ milkshake flavors, often visited by upperclassmen with vehicle privileges.
cards.short_summary: A classic Southern fast-food chain offering budget-friendly trays and milkshakes until the early morning.
cards.evidence_claim: Cook Out locations typically operate until 3:30 AM or 4:30 AM, serving as a primary late-night food source.
cards.source_title: Cookout Hours | What Time Does Cook Out Open & Close?
cards.access_notes: Open until 3:30 AM or later daily.

cards.title: The 24-Hour Safety Net
cards.subtitle: Savannah Highway
cards.notes: When all other options fail, Waffle House provides 24/7 service. It is a common meeting point for cadets on overnight leave or those needing a meal at any hour.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour diner chain that is a reliable late-night option for students and cadets in Charleston.
cards.evidence_claim: Waffle House locations in Charleston are open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.
cards.source_title: Waffle House #233
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7.

cards.title: The Window Order
cards.subtitle: Spring Street
cards.notes: Known for authentic Philly-style cheesesteaks, this walk-up window is a favorite for quick, late-night fuel. Cadets often stop here while navigating the downtown area.
cards.short_summary: A late-night cheesesteak shop offering authentic Philly-style subs through a walk-up window.
cards.evidence_claim: South Street Cheesesteaks is open daily from 9:00 AM to 3:00 AM.
cards.source_title: South Street Cheesesteaks and Subs
cards.access_notes: Open until 3:00 AM daily.

cards.title: The Study Grind Hub
cards.subtitle: Mark Clark Hall
cards.notes: The primary caffeine source on campus, this Starbucks provides a space for cadets to study and socialize during the day and early evening hours.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus Starbucks location providing coffee and snacks to the Corps of Cadets.
cards.evidence_claim: Starbucks is located on the 1st floor of Mark Clark Hall on The Citadel campus.
cards.source_title: Retail Dining - Auxiliary Services - The Citadel
cards.access_notes: Typically open until 7:00 PM on weekdays.

cards.title: The Historic Snack Bar
cards.subtitle: Mark Clark Hall
cards.notes: Also known as the Munnerlyn Snack Bar, it offers deli sandwiches and flatbread pizzas. It is a traditional spot where cadets grab quick meals between duties.
cards.short_summary: A campus dining staple offering affordable deli and pizza options to the Citadel community.
cards.evidence_claim: The Canteen (Munnerlyn Snack Bar) is located on campus and serves breakfast and lunch items.
cards.source_title: The Canteen - The Citadel Campus
cards.access_notes: Primarily a breakfast and lunch destination; hours vary by semester.

cards.title: The Huger Street Hangout
cards.subtitle: Huger Street
cards.notes: Located near the campus gates, Taco Boy is a popular spot for cadets on leave to enjoy tacos and a vibrant atmosphere before returning to the barracks.
cards.short_summary: A lively Mexican-inspired restaurant located just outside the Citadel's campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Boy is located at 217 Huger Street and is a known dining spot for the local community.
cards.source_title: Taco Boy Charleston
cards.access_notes: Open until 11:00 PM or midnight on weekends.

cards.title: The Walkable Dinner
cards.subtitle: Rutledge Avenue
cards.notes: One of the few restaurants within genuine walking distance of campus, Berkeley's offers sandwiches and comfort food for cadets on short leave windows.
cards.short_summary: A neighborhood restaurant near The Citadel known for its sandwiches and proximity to campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Berkeley's is noted as a walkable dining option from The Citadel campus.
cards.source_title: The Citadel Guide: Where to Eat, Drink & Stay in Charleston (2026)
cards.access_notes: Open for dinner; check seasonal hours for late-night availability.

cards.title: The King Street Nacho Run
cards.subtitle: King Street
cards.notes: A King Street mainstay for affordable Mexican-style food, this spot is a frequent late-night choice for students and cadets looking for a casual meal.
cards.short_summary: A casual Mexican restaurant on King Street popular for its late-night nacho and taco offerings.
cards.evidence_claim: Juanita Greenberg's is open daily until 2:00 AM.
cards.source_title: Juanita Greenberg's Nacho Royale
cards.access_notes: Open until 2:00 AM daily.

boards.school_name: Citadel Military College of South Carolina
boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the functional study hubs, recreational retreats, and quiet corners that Citadel cadets and students use to navigate their daily military and academic schedules.

cards.title: Collaborative Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Daniel Library
cards.notes: Reserve one of the four collaborative study rooms for group projects or quiet focus. Check in at the Information Desk to access your booked space.
cards.short_summary: Private group study rooms available for reservation within the main campus library.
cards.evidence_claim: Daniel Library facilities include four collaborative study rooms and the Prioleau Reading Room for student use.
cards.source_title: Daniel Library & The Citadel Museum
cards.access_notes: Rooms must be vacated before library closing; current library card or ID required for reservation.

cards.title: Kerr Reading Room
cards.subtitle: 261 Bond Hall
cards.notes: Visit this quiet study space featuring a large projection screen for presentations and three private study rooms equipped with monitors.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated quiet study and group meeting area located on the second floor of Bond Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The Kerr Reading Room in 261 Bond Hall provides students with quiet study space and private rooms with 32-inch monitors.
cards.source_title: Student Resources - Master of Business Administration
cards.access_notes: Open every school day; primarily serves business students but offers a central workstation for presentations.

cards.title: Class of 1981 Pavilion
cards.subtitle: Waterfront at Ashley River
cards.notes: Relax by the gas log fireplace or use the charcoal grills at this waterfront pavilion. It is a shared recreational space for the entire community.
cards.short_summary: A waterfront recreational pavilion featuring a fireplace and grills for student and faculty use.
cards.evidence_claim: The Class of 1981 Pavilion at the Swain Boating Center features a gas log fireplace, picnic tables, and charcoal grills.
cards.source_title: Hours of Operation - Swain Boating Center
cards.access_notes: Normal operating hours are 0800-2000 daily; users are responsible for cleanup of grills.

cards.title: Recreational Fitness Center
cards.subtitle: Deas Hall
cards.notes: Access the 25-meter pool, racquetball courts, and strength training facilities. Remember to wear appropriate gym attire and bring your ID.
cards.short_summary: The primary campus hub for intramural sports, swimming, and individual weight training.
cards.evidence_claim: Deas Hall houses an eight-lane swimming pool, six racquetball courts, and a 14,500-square-foot gymnasium.
cards.source_title: Deas Hall Membership - Intramural, Club and Recreational Athletics
cards.access_notes: Priority use for students and ROTC; membership card required for entry.

cards.title: Munnerlyn Food Court
cards.subtitle: Student Activities Building
cards.notes: Grab a quick meal at this full-service snack bar. It serves as a central social hub for cadets between classes and training.
cards.short_summary: A central campus dining and social area located within the student activities building.
cards.evidence_claim: Mark Clark Hall houses the Munnerlyn Food Court, a full-service snack bar open to the public and students.
cards.source_title: Mark Clark Hall - Brand Guidelines
cards.access_notes: Open to the public; houses the campus bookstore and student services.

cards.title: Mathematics Lab
cards.subtitle: Student Success Center
cards.notes: Drop in for academic coaching or use the specialized math and computer labs. It is the go-to spot for supplemental instruction.
cards.short_summary: An academic support hub providing tutoring and specialized computer labs for students.
cards.evidence_claim: Thompson Hall is home to the Student Success Center, which includes a Mathematics Lab and several computer labs.
cards.source_title: Thompson Hall - The Citadel Campus
cards.access_notes: Located in Room 117; appointments can be made via email or phone.

cards.title: Gothic Sanctuary
cards.subtitle: Avenue of Remembrance
cards.notes: Find a moment of quiet reflection among the 14th-century Gothic architecture and handcrafted wrought iron fixtures.
cards.short_summary: A non-denominational chapel used for religious services, weddings, and quiet meditation.
cards.evidence_claim: Summerall Chapel is a cruciform, non-denominational chapel that supports students through religious expression and counseling.
cards.source_title: History - Summerall Chapel
cards.access_notes: Open for weekly worship services and special events; accessible to the broader community.

cards.title: Bastin Financial Lab
cards.subtitle: Baker School of Business
cards.notes: Experience a simulated trading floor with dual-monitor terminals and a 22-foot color ticker display. Ideal for finance students.
cards.short_summary: A state-of-the-art financial simulation lab with real-world data and analytical tools.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bastin Financial Lab features 29 computer terminals, a full-color ticker display, and a 92-inch LED market video wall.
cards.source_title: Student Resources - Master of Business Administration
cards.access_notes: Used extensively by the Financial Management Association; check for lab availability.

cards.title: McKissick Library
cards.subtitle: Hagood Avenue
cards.notes: Utilize this quiet library space located just off the main campus. It is a useful alternative for study when the main library is busy.
cards.short_summary: A secondary library and visitor center located within the alumni complex.
cards.evidence_claim: The Holliday Alumni Center houses the McKissick Library, a grand foyer, and visitor center.
cards.source_title: The John Monroe Johnson Holliday Alumni Center
cards.access_notes: Located across from the football stadium; serves as a staging area for visitors and alumni.

cards.title: Bulldog Student Section
cards.subtitle: Sansom Field
cards.notes: Join the Corps of Cadets in the stands for home football games. Experience the electric atmosphere of Southern Conference matchups.
cards.short_summary: The home field for Citadel football, featuring a dedicated section for the Corps of Cadets.
cards.evidence_claim: Johnson Hagood Stadium is the home of Citadel football, where the student section and alumni bring energy to every game.
cards.source_title: Johnson Hagood Stadium - Facilities
cards.access_notes: Cadet attendance is often mandatory for home games; public tickets require purchase.

boards.school_name: Citadel Military College of South Carolina
boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Discover free social spaces and activities at The Citadel, from historic museum galleries and scenic riverfront parks to iconic military parades open to the public.

cards.title: Watch a Dress Parade
cards.subtitle: Summerall Field
cards.notes: Observe the South Carolina Corps of Cadets march in formation most Fridays at 3:45 PM. It is free to watch from the bleachers; arrive early for parking.
cards.short_summary: Attend a traditional military dress parade featuring the Regimental Band and Pipes on the main campus parade ground.
cards.evidence_claim: Citadel parades are free to attend and open to the public.
cards.source_title: The Citadel Parades - The Citadel Regimental Band and Pipes
cards.access_notes: Open to the public on scheduled Fridays during the academic year; check the online schedule for specific dates.

cards.title: Explore Citadel History
cards.subtitle: Daniel Library, 3rd Floor
cards.notes: View uniforms, class rings, and military artifacts tracing the college's history since 1842. Located on the third floor of the library with no admission fee.
cards.short_summary: A campus museum showcasing the military, academic, and social history of The Citadel through various exhibits.
cards.evidence_claim: The Citadel Museum opened in 1960 and is located on the third floor of the library building... Admission is free.
cards.source_title: Daniel Library & The Citadel Museum
cards.access_notes: Open to the public during library hours, typically weekdays from 7:30 AM to 9:00 PM.

cards.title: Visit Summerall Chapel
cards.subtitle: Avenue of Remembrance
cards.notes: Step inside this historic cruciform chapel to see the regimental colors and stained glass. It serves as a quiet space for reflection and community worship.
cards.short_summary: A non-denominational shrine and place of worship on campus known for its beautiful architecture and military flags.
cards.evidence_claim: Summerall Chapel advocates for religious expression by supporting students, faculty, staff and the greater Charleston community.
cards.source_title: Summerall Chapel - The Citadel
cards.access_notes: Generally open to visitors during the day; Sunday services are held at 9:00 AM.

cards.title: Relax at Hampton Park
cards.subtitle: Adjacent to Campus
cards.notes: Walk or run the trails at this 60-acre park located right next to campus. It features extensive floral displays and a physical fitness trail used by cadets.
cards.short_summary: One of Charleston's largest public parks, offering green space, gardens, and trails immediately beside The Citadel.
cards.evidence_claim: The physical fitness trail is a popular spot for The Citadel students who live next door to the park... Grounds are free.
cards.source_title: Hampton Park - Facilities • Charleston, SC
cards.access_notes: Public park open daily from dawn to dusk; vehicles restricted during specific 'Walk, Run & Roll' hours.

cards.title: Study in Daniel Library
cards.subtitle: Avenue of Remembrance
cards.notes: Utilize collaborative study rooms or the Prioleau Reading Room for quiet work. The library serves as the campus information hub with free access for students.
cards.short_summary: The primary academic library on campus offering various study spaces and historical collections.
cards.evidence_claim: Facilities include four collaborative study rooms, two classrooms, and the Prioleau Reading Room.
cards.source_title: Daniel Library & The Citadel Museum
cards.access_notes: Open to students and the public; typical hours are 7:30 AM to 9:00 PM on weekdays.

cards.title: Access the Beach
cards.subtitle: Isle of Palms
cards.notes: Cadets and students can access the beach and use the outdoor facilities at this off-campus property. Parking is available for the Citadel family.
cards.short_summary: A college-owned oceanfront venue on Isle of Palms where students can enjoy beach access and outdoor amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: Beach access will continue to be available for The Citadel Family, regardless of the event booked in the Ballroom or Pavilion.
cards.source_title: Frequently Asked Questions - The Citadel Beach Club
cards.access_notes: Restricted to the Citadel family (students, faculty, staff, and alumni); not open to the general public.

cards.title: Workout at Deas Hall
cards.subtitle: Campus Fitness Center
cards.notes: Use the cardio and weight rooms or register for a free locker to store your gear. This facility is the hub for intramural and recreational athletics.
cards.short_summary: The campus recreation center providing fitness equipment and locker facilities for the student body.
cards.evidence_claim: There is no fee to use a locker; however, lockers must be registered in the First Floor Equipment Room.
cards.source_title: Students - Intramural, Club and Recreational Athletics - The Citadel
cards.access_notes: Open to students with valid ID; users must provide their own locks for the free lockers.

cards.title: Stroll the Riverfront
cards.subtitle: West Side of Campus
cards.notes: Walk along the banks of the Ashley River for scenic views of the water and the Swain Boating Center. A peaceful spot for a sunset walk.
cards.short_summary: The scenic western edge of campus bordering the Ashley River, offering paths and water views.
cards.evidence_claim: Stroll our scenic riverfront campus or explore it online.
cards.source_title: Visit The Citadel
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible campus grounds open year-round.

cards.title: Hang Out in Mark Clark Hall
cards.subtitle: Student Union
cards.notes: Gather in the lounge areas or the auditorium of the student union. It houses the bookstore and dining options, but the common spaces are free to use.
cards.short_summary: The central student activity building on campus with lounges and meeting spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: In Spring 2026, we will be worshipping in the Mark Clark Hall Auditorium... MCH is the building just past the Chapel.
cards.source_title: FAQs — TCSC - The Church at Summerall Chapel
cards.access_notes: Open daily; serves as a primary gathering spot for cadets during free time.

cards.title: Visit the War Memorial
cards.subtitle: Near Summerall Field
cards.notes: Pay respects at this monument dedicated to Citadel alumni who gave their lives in service. It is an outdoor site accessible to all visitors.
cards.short_summary: A solemn campus landmark honoring the sacrifices of Citadel graduates in various military conflicts.
cards.evidence_claim: Explore campus landmarks... Discover iconic landmarks like Summerall Chapel, the Daniel Library and The Citadel Museum.
cards.source_title: Visitor Information - Visit The Citadel
cards.access_notes: Outdoor memorial open to the public 24/7.

boards.school_name: Citadel Military College of South Carolina

cards.subtitle: Daniel Library
cards.notes: Reserve one of the four collaborative study rooms for group projects. These spaces are equipped with technology to support team-based academic work.
cards.short_summary: Reservable group study rooms in the main campus library.
cards.evidence_claim: Daniel Library features four collaborative study rooms and a Zoom interview/online exam space available for student booking.
cards.source_title: Space Availability - Daniel Library
cards.access_notes: Open during library operating hours; reservations are recommended via the LibCal system.

cards.title: Historic Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Daniel Library
cards.notes: Study surrounded by Citadel history in this quiet room housing yearbooks and historic publications. It offers a traditional academic atmosphere.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, historic reading room located within Daniel Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Prioleau Reading Room houses Citadel yearbooks and other historic publications for student use.
cards.source_title: Daniel Library & The Citadel Museum

cards.title: Bastin Hall Atrium
cards.subtitle: Baker School of Business
cards.notes: Utilize the open atrium for casual study between classes. This modern space is a central hub for business students and features ample natural light.
cards.short_summary: A large, modern common area for studying in the business school.
cards.evidence_claim: Bastin Hall features large common areas and an atrium typically used by students for studying.
cards.source_title: Bastin Hall - The Citadel
cards.access_notes: Open to students during academic building hours.

cards.title: Financial Trading Lab

cards.notes: Access Bloomberg terminals and real-time market data in this state-of-the-art lab. Ideal for finance students needing specialized software.
cards.short_summary: A high-tech lab simulating a real trading floor with 29 computer terminals.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bastin Financial Lab features 29 computer terminals, a 22-foot ticker display, and access to financial data tools.
cards.source_title: Bastin Hall - The Citadel

cards.title: Kerr Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Bond Hall 261
cards.notes: Find a quiet spot or meet for group work in this dedicated business student space. It includes private study rooms with monitors for project review.
cards.short_summary: A quiet study and meeting space for business students in Bond Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The Kerr Reading Room in Bond Hall 261 provides quiet study space and three private study rooms with monitors.
cards.source_title: Student Resources - The Citadel
cards.access_notes: Open every school day for business students.

cards.title: Mathematics Lab
cards.subtitle: Thompson Hall
cards.notes: Get help with difficult problem sets or study in a focused environment. The lab provides specialized support for math and data analytics.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated lab for mathematics study and tutoring support.
cards.evidence_claim: Thompson Hall houses the Mathematics Lab, providing academic support and study space for students.
cards.source_title: Department of Mathematical Sciences
cards.access_notes: Check the Student Success Center website for current lab hours.

cards.entity_name: Angela W. Williams Student Success Center
cards.title: Student Success Center
cards.subtitle: Thompson Hall 117
cards.notes: Visit for academic coaching or subject-area tutoring. It is a welcoming environment designed to help students excel academically.
cards.short_summary: A comprehensive academic support hub with various study resources.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Success Center (SSC) in Thompson Hall 117 offers academic coaching, tutoring, and a writing lab.
cards.source_title: Student Success Center - The Citadel
cards.access_notes: Appointments are recommended; walk-ins are welcome during operating hours.

cards.title: Legal Studies Classroom
cards.subtitle: School of Humanities
cards.notes: Study in a unique mock courtroom environment. This new facility is ideal for pre-law students and those in the School of Humanities.
cards.short_summary: A state-of-the-art mock courtroom used for classes and study.
cards.evidence_claim: The new Capers Hall includes a Legal Studies classroom designed as a mock courtroom for student use.
cards.source_title: The Citadel's New Capers Hall
cards.access_notes: Accessible during building hours when classes are not in session.

cards.title: Starbucks Study Lounge
cards.subtitle: Mark Clark Hall
cards.notes: Enjoy a coffee while you work in this social study spot. It's a popular choice for students who prefer a bit of background noise.
cards.short_summary: A full-service Starbucks with seating areas inside the student union.
cards.evidence_claim: Mark Clark Hall houses a full-service Starbucks Coffee and common areas for students.
cards.source_title: Mark Clark Hall - The Citadel
cards.access_notes: Open during retail dining hours; seating is available for studying.

cards.title: Bond Café Seating
cards.subtitle: Bond Hall
cards.notes: Grab a hot meal and find a table for a quiet study session. This café offers a more relaxed alternative to the main mess hall.
cards.short_summary: A quiet dining and study area located in historic Bond Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Bond Hall is home to Bond Café, which offers a quiet, hot meal and seating for students.
cards.source_title: Bond Hall - The Citadel
cards.access_notes: Accessible during café operating hours.

boards.school_name: Citadel Military College of South Carolina
boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Explore the corridors and micro-districts surrounding The Citadel, from the quiet fitness trails of Hampton Park to the bustling dining hubs of Upper King and Rutledge Avenue.

cards.title: The 1-Mile Loop
cards.subtitle: Mary Murray Drive
cards.notes: Run the scenic 1-mile loop bordering campus. This paved trail is a standard off-duty exercise spot for cadets and local joggers under moss-draped oaks.
cards.short_summary: A popular 1-mile fitness loop and arboretum located immediately adjacent to The Citadel's eastern border.
cards.evidence_claim: The physical fitness trail is a popular spot for The Citadel students who live next door to the park.
cards.source_title: Hampton Park - Facilities • Charleston, SC
cards.access_notes: Open daily from sunrise to sunset.

cards.title: The Walkable Dinner
cards.subtitle: Rutledge Avenue
cards.notes: Visit one of the few genuinely walkable dining spots from campus. This corridor serves as a primary destination for cadets on short off-campus passes.
cards.short_summary: A neighborhood dining corridor on Rutledge Avenue featuring student-accessible eateries within walking distance of the barracks.
cards.evidence_claim: Berkeley's is the one place on this list you can genuinely walk to from campus.
cards.source_title: The Citadel Guide: Where to Eat, Drink & Stay in Charleston (2026)
cards.access_notes: Check individual business hours; generally open for lunch and dinner.

cards.title: The Culinary Artery
cards.subtitle: King Street (North of Calhoun)
cards.notes: Explore the densest concentration of independent restaurants in the city. It is a major weekend hub for students seeking food beyond the mess hall.
cards.short_summary: A vibrant commercial district north of Calhoun Street known for its high density of independent restaurants and shops.
cards.evidence_claim: Upper King starts somewhere around Calhoun Street and Marion Square and runs north from there... the density of independent restaurants increases noticeably.
cards.source_title: The Complete Walking Guide to Upper King Street, Charleston
cards.access_notes: Public street; most businesses open late into the evening.

cards.title: The Emerging Mecca
cards.subtitle: Cannon Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk through this evolving district for coffee and unique retail. It is a popular residential and social pocket for the local student population.
cards.short_summary: A historic neighborhood corridor featuring a mix of coffee shops, bakeries, and student-oriented housing.
cards.evidence_claim: Cannon Street and Spring Street... is undeniably one of the fastest and most emerging urban communities... made up of a mix of tourists, students and residents.
cards.source_title: An Insider's Guide to Upper King Street
cards.access_notes: Public neighborhood; best explored during daylight and early evening hours.

cards.title: The North Morrison Hub
cards.subtitle: Morrison Drive
cards.notes: Head to the 'NoMo' district for modern student living and industrial-chic eateries. This area has become a primary off-campus residential anchor.
cards.short_summary: An industrial-turned-residential district on the upper peninsula popular for student housing and creative offices.
cards.evidence_claim: In the lively NoMo district, close to campus and Charleston's best, 930 NoMo keeps everything within reach at 930 Morrison Dr.
cards.source_title: 930 NoMo: Premier Student Apartments in Charleston
cards.access_notes: Residential area with public-facing retail and dining.

cards.title: The Student Thoroughfare
cards.subtitle: St. Philip Street
cards.notes: Navigate this north-south street to find major student housing complexes and local cafes. It serves as a central spine for the downtown academic community.
cards.short_summary: A key street connecting the mid-peninsula to the upper districts, lined with student apartments and academic buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: 99 St. Philip Street is a co-ed... four-story building at the corner of St. Philip and Vanderhorst streets.
cards.source_title: 99 St. Philip Street - College of Charleston
cards.access_notes: Public thoroughfare; residential buildings require student ID for entry.

cards.title: The Meeting Street Spine
cards.subtitle: Meeting Street
cards.notes: Check out the northern stretch of Meeting Street for large-scale student housing and quick-service dining options near the Ravenel Bridge.
cards.short_summary: A major arterial road featuring significant off-campus housing developments and commercial services.
cards.evidence_claim: Summit Place provides apartments for rent... located at 530 Meeting St Charleston, SC 29403.
cards.source_title: Summit Place | Apartments in Charleston, SC
cards.access_notes: Public street; residential amenities restricted to residents.

cards.title: The Waterfront Edge
cards.subtitle: East Bay Street
cards.notes: Visit the eastern edge of the peninsula for harbor views and new student developments. This area offers a quieter alternative to the central King Street buzz.
cards.short_summary: A scenic waterfront corridor on the east side of the peninsula featuring historic sites and new residential projects.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mark Charleston... will be built at 500 East Bay Street on the east side of the peninsula.
cards.source_title: HP and LP Announce Charleston Student Housing Development
cards.access_notes: Public street with waterfront access nearby.

cards.title: The Riverfront Escape
cards.subtitle: Lockwood Boulevard
cards.notes: Walk to the riverfront for sunset views and pier fishing. Located just south of campus, it provides a wide-open green space for outdoor recreation.
cards.short_summary: A 10-acre riverfront park offering a fishing pier, playground, and views of the Ashley River.
cards.evidence_claim: Enjoy... sunset views at Brittlebank Park.
cards.source_title: Brittlebank Park - Facilities • Charleston, SC
cards.access_notes: Open daily from 6:00 AM to 11:00 PM.

cards.title: The Ballpark Block
cards.subtitle: Fishburne Street
cards.notes: Catch a RiverDogs game at 'The Joe.' This stadium block is a major local entertainment draw within walking distance of the campus gates.
cards.short_summary: The home stadium of the Charleston RiverDogs, located on the banks of the Ashley River near The Citadel.
cards.evidence_claim: Catch a Charleston RiverDogs baseball game at Joseph P. Riley Jr. Park.
cards.source_title: Joseph P. Riley, Jr. Park Guide | Charleston RiverDogs
cards.access_notes: Open during scheduled games and events; ticket required for entry.

boards.school_name: Citadel Military College of South Carolina
boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Explore the unique military rituals, historic symbols, and rigorous milestones that define the cadet experience at The Citadel.

cards.title: The Silent Drill
cards.subtitle: A precision drill platoon founded in 1932
cards.notes: Watch the elite 61-member silent drill platoon perform complex maneuvers based on Prussian drills without a single spoken command.
cards.short_summary: The Summerall Guards are an elite silent precision drill platoon that performs complex maneuvers to a silent count.
cards.evidence_claim: The Summerall Guards were created in 1932 and perform unique maneuvers based on old Prussian drills that have never been written down.
cards.source_title: The Summerall Guards - The Citadel
cards.access_notes: Performances typically occur during Friday dress parades and special events on Summerall Field.

cards.title: The Band of Gold
cards.subtitle: A symbol of the Long Gray Line
cards.notes: Observe seniors receiving their heavy gold rings, featuring symbols like the Star of the West and the Palmetto tree.
cards.short_summary: The Citadel Ring is a highly symbolic piece of jewelry awarded to seniors who meet rigorous academic and military requirements.
cards.evidence_claim: The Citadel has only two official designed rings (cadet and non-cadet) and the presentation is a major annual milestone for the graduating class.
cards.source_title: The Ring - The Citadel Alumni Association
cards.access_notes: The ceremony is held annually in McAlister Field House for the senior class and their families.

cards.title: The End of Knob Year
cards.subtitle: Transitioning from Knob to Cadet
cards.notes: Witness the culmination of the Fourth-Class System as freshmen complete 'The Gauntlet' and are finally called by their first names.
cards.short_summary: Recognition Day marks the official end of the highly regimented Fourth-Class System for freshmen, known as Knobs.
cards.evidence_claim: Recognition Day involves intense physical challenges followed by a formal announcement that the Fourth-Class system is no longer in effect.
cards.source_title: Recognition Day - Annual Events - The Citadel
cards.access_notes: The event takes place across campus and in the barracks; public viewing is available for the subsequent parade.

cards.title: The Long Gray Line
cards.subtitle: Weekly military review on Summerall Field
cards.notes: Attend a traditional military review featuring the entire Corps of Cadets marching in formation with the Regimental Band.
cards.short_summary: The Friday Dress Parade is a weekly public event where the Corps of Cadets demonstrates precision marching and military honors.
cards.evidence_claim: Citadel parades are held on Summerall Field most Fridays during the academic year and are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Parade Schedule - Visit The Citadel
cards.access_notes: Parades typically begin at 1545 (3:45 PM) on scheduled Fridays; visitors should arrive early for parking.

cards.title: The Spirit of Big Red
cards.subtitle: The official flag of the Corps of Cadets
cards.notes: Look for the red flag with a white palmetto and crescent, a historic symbol flown by cadets during the Civil War.
cards.short_summary: Big Red is the distinctive red palmetto flag that serves as the official spirit flag for The Citadel's Corps of Cadets.
cards.evidence_claim: Big Red is an official flag of the Corps, symbolizing duty and honor, and is flown at major sporting events and parades.
cards.source_title: Big Red Flag - The Citadel Alumni Association
cards.access_notes: The flag is visible at all home football games and formal military dress parades on campus.

cards.title: The Live Mascot
cards.subtitle: A tradition of English Bulldogs since 1908
cards.notes: Meet the current live mascot, General, who lives on campus in a custom-built house and attends major college events.
cards.short_summary: The Citadel maintains a live English Bulldog mascot program, with the dogs cared for by a dedicated cadet handling team.
cards.evidence_claim: The live mascot program was formalized by the Class of 2003, and the bulldogs reside on campus in a dedicated facility.
cards.source_title: Citadel Live Mascot Team - Cadet Activities
cards.access_notes: General is often seen at Johnson Hagood Stadium during games and near McAlister Field House.

cards.title: The Best Drilled Cadet
cards.subtitle: An individual drill competition since 1886
cards.notes: Observe the annual competition where cadets compete for the prestigious medal containing wood from the historic ship.
cards.short_summary: The Star of the West is an annual individual drill competition that awards the best-drilled cadet in the Corps.
cards.evidence_claim: The competition has been a tradition since 1886 and the winner's name is inscribed on a monument on Summerall Field.
cards.source_title: Cadet Kyle O'Grady wins 2026 Star of the West competition
cards.access_notes: The competition is held annually in May on Summerall Field and is open to public spectators.

cards.title: The Doorknob Look
cards.subtitle: The signature haircut of first-year cadets
cards.notes: Learn about the 'Knob' nickname, derived from the closely shorn heads of freshmen that resemble doorknobs.
cards.short_summary: Freshmen at The Citadel are called 'Knobs' due to the mandatory short haircuts they receive upon matriculation.
cards.evidence_claim: Male fourth-class cadets receive an initial haircut at matriculation, a tradition that gives them their 'Knob' moniker.
cards.source_title: Citadel changes grooming policy to match DOD standards
cards.access_notes: Visible on all first-year cadets throughout the campus during the academic year.

cards.title: The Annual Muster
cards.subtitle: Honoring the Long Gray Line every March 20th
cards.notes: Join alumni worldwide as they gather to answer the roll call for classmates who have passed away in the previous year.
cards.short_summary: The Muster is a solemn annual tradition held on Corps Day to honor deceased alumni of The Citadel.
cards.evidence_claim: The Muster is held annually on March 20th (Corps Day) by alumni clubs worldwide to recognize fallen members of the Long Gray Line.
cards.source_title: The Citadel Muster - The Citadel Alumni Association
cards.access_notes: The main campus muster is held at the Holliday Alumni Center; other musters occur globally.

cards.title: Lights in the Chapel
cards.subtitle: A musical holiday tradition in Summerall Chapel
cards.notes: Experience a historic Charleston holiday event featuring cadet choirs and the Regimental Band in a candlelit chapel.
cards.short_summary: The Christmas Candlelight Service is a long-standing holiday tradition featuring music and scripture in the historic Summerall Chapel.
cards.evidence_claim: The service is held for three consecutive nights in December and includes a Procession of Lights by the cadets.
cards.source_title: Christmas Candlelight Services at Summerall Chapel - The Citadel
cards.access_notes: Held annually in early December; the event is open to the public but seating is limited.

boards.school_name: Citadel Military College of South Carolina
boards.title: Your First Weekend at Citadel Military College of South Carolina, Shared as Cards
boards.description: Build a plausible under-21-safe first-weekend sequence, not a ranking. Give each card one role in the sequence and use evergreen places or recurring behaviors rather than one-time events. Be conservative about hours, access, and travel time unless directly sourced.

cards.title: Check In for Matriculation
cards.subtitle: The Starting Point
cards.notes: Report here on Saturday morning to receive your company and room assignments. This is where your transition from civilian to cadet-recruit officially begins.
cards.short_summary: The primary processing center for incoming cadet-recruits on Matriculation Day.
cards.evidence_claim: Processing for members of the Class of 2029 will begin at the Holliday Alumni Center, where they will receive company and room assignments.
cards.source_title: 2025-26 Event Calendar - The Citadel Today
cards.access_notes: Open early on Matriculation Day for scheduled check-ins; typically 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM weekdays.

cards.title: Move Into the Barracks
cards.subtitle: Your New Home
cards.notes: Unload your gear and meet your classmates in the barracks. Expect a busy day of uniform issues and initial military instruction within these historic walls.
cards.short_summary: The residential quarters where all members of the Corps of Cadets live during the academic year.
cards.evidence_claim: Matriculation Day is the day you move into the barracks and start developing a lifelong bond with your classmates.
cards.source_title: Matriculation Headquarters - The Citadel
cards.access_notes: Restricted to cadets and staff; visitors require a cadet escort and are limited to specific family weekends.

cards.title: First Meal at the Mess Hall
cards.subtitle: Family-Style Dining
cards.notes: Experience your first mandatory formation and family-style meal. This massive hall serves the entire Corps of Cadets with high-protein and low-country options.
cards.short_summary: The central dining facility for the Corps of Cadets, known as the Mess Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The entire first floor consists of the dining area, or 'mess hall' as the cadets call it, that serves the entire Corps of Cadets for family-style meals.
cards.source_title: Coward Hall (Mess Hall) - The Citadel Campus
cards.access_notes: Open for mandatory cadet meal formations; guests must wear appropriate civilian attire and sit on the South side.

cards.title: Observe a Practice Parade
cards.subtitle: Precision on the Field
cards.notes: Watch the Corps of Cadets practice drill maneuvers on this 10-acre parade ground. It is the heart of the campus and the site of weekly Friday dress parades.
cards.short_summary: The iconic parade ground used for military reviews, drills, and ceremonial events.
cards.evidence_claim: Citadel parades are held on Summerall Field most Fridays during the academic year and are open to the public.
cards.source_title: Parade Schedule - Visit The Citadel
cards.access_notes: Open to the public for parades; typically held at 3:45 PM on scheduled Fridays.

cards.title: Attend Sunday Morning Worship
cards.subtitle: Spiritual Reflection
cards.notes: Join the intergenerational community for a non-denominational service at 9 AM. It is a quiet space for reflection before the rigors of the week begin.
cards.short_summary: A historic campus landmark hosting religious services and community gatherings.
cards.evidence_claim: The Church at Summerall Chapel (TCSC) is a non-denominational Christian service held on Sunday mornings at 9 AM.
cards.source_title: Worship at Summerall Chapel - The Citadel
cards.access_notes: Sunday services at 9 AM and 5 PM; open to cadets, students, and the public.

cards.title: Explore Academic Resources
cards.subtitle: Study and Research
cards.notes: Visit the library to find study spaces, research assistance, and the campus museum. It is a vital resource for your academic success as a new cadet.
cards.short_summary: The primary academic library providing resources, study areas, and historical archives.
cards.evidence_claim: The Library is a very helpful asset on campus, providing resources, services, programs and staff to support the educational needs.
cards.source_title: Student Services & Organizations - The Citadel Graduate College
cards.access_notes: Open Sunday 1 PM - 9 PM and weekdays 7:30 AM - 9 PM during the academic year.

cards.title: Learn Citadel History
cards.subtitle: The Long Gray Line
cards.notes: Located on the third floor of Daniel Library, this museum showcases the history of the college since 1842 through uniforms and archival documents.
cards.short_summary: A museum dedicated to preserving and displaying the history and traditions of The Citadel.
cards.evidence_claim: Museum portrays the history of the school from 1842 to present with photographs, uniforms and archival documents.
cards.source_title: The Citadel Museum | Charleston, SC
cards.access_notes: Open Sunday - Friday 2 PM to 5 PM, and Saturday 12 PM to 5 PM.

cards.title: Visit the Student Union
cards.subtitle: Campus Hub
cards.notes: Stop by to visit the bookstore, grab a coffee at Starbucks, or visit the post office. It serves as the primary social and service hub for students.
cards.short_summary: The student union building housing the bookstore, dining options, and student services.
cards.evidence_claim: Mark Clark Hall... housing the Starbucks and Bookstore. The Auditorium is located immediately up the main staircase.
cards.source_title: FAQs — TCSC - The Church at Summerall Chapel
cards.access_notes: General campus hours; bookstore open 8 AM to 4 PM on game days.

cards.title: Attend a Football Game
cards.subtitle: Bulldog Spirit
cards.notes: Join the Corps in the student section to cheer on the Bulldogs. The stadium offers an authentic college football experience right on the edge of campus.
cards.short_summary: The home stadium for The Citadel Bulldogs football team.
cards.evidence_claim: Johnson Hagood Stadium is the home of The Citadel Bulldogs football team... The student section, alumni, and local supporters bring energy.
cards.source_title: Johnson Hagood Stadium: SeatGeek's complete guide
cards.access_notes: Gates typically open two hours prior to kick-off; student access via designated gates.

cards.title: Freshman Beach Day
cards.subtitle: Off-Campus Excursion
cards.notes: Participate in the traditional beach trip to Isle of Palms. It is a rare opportunity for new cadet-recruits to relax and bond outside the campus gates.
cards.short_summary: A private beach facility on Isle of Palms for use by the Citadel community.
cards.evidence_claim: Cadet recruits enjoy a picnic at the Citadel Beach House at the conclusion of Challenge Week.
cards.source_title: The Citadel - Class of 2023 Beach Day photos
cards.access_notes: Located 15 miles from campus; intended for recreational use by cadets, students, and alumni.
